observations: Three photos show multiple electronic keyboards wrapped in plastic, standing upright on a tiled floor.
The keyboards have 61 keys, typical of portable or mini keyboards.
The keyboards vary in design: some have a black and white color scheme, others are silver or light gray, and one has a blue and white panel with a control wheel and buttons.
The plastic wrapping is crinkled and appears to be new or lightly used.
No brand or model name is visible on any keyboard in any photo.
The background includes a wall with a pipe and a fan, suggesting a storage or workshop area.
The watermark 'MARY OLUGBAMI POSTED ON JIJI' is present on all photos.

claims.evidence: No brand or model is visible to assess quality or price. The term 'quality' is subjective and cannot be verified from photos alone.

risks.proof: A video showing the keyboard powered on, keys responding, and sound output.

risks.risk: The keyboards may be counterfeit or rebranded, not genuine.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the brand name and model number on the keyboard, preferably from the back or underside.

risks.risk: The keyboards may be damaged or have missing parts (e.g., power adapter, stand, or accessories).

A clear photo of the brand and model name on the keyboard, preferably from the back or underside.
